title: Cursor Rules (.mdc), copilot-instructions.md & GEMINI.md
description: Side-by-side guide to .cursor/rules/*.mdc frontmatter, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and GEMINI.md for coding assistant instructions.
dek: Every IDE and terminal agent has its own instruction file path and frontmatter syntax. Here is the exact format for Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex.
lede: If you switch between Cursor, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex, you have probably noticed that each tool looks for a different Markdown file. Fortunately, the communication preferences block itself is identical across all five; only the file path and optional YAML header change.
answer: Put always-on Cursor communication rules in .cursor/rules/agenttune.mdc with alwaysApply: true in the YAML frontmatter. For GitHub Copilot, append your section to .github/copilot-instructions.md. For Gemini CLI and Code Assist, use ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md (personal) or repo GEMINI.md. For Claude Code, use ~/.claude/output-styles/agenttune.md or CLAUDE.md. For OpenAI Codex, use ~/.codex/AGENTS.md.

Cursor replaced the older single .cursorrules file with modular .mdc files inside .cursor/rules/. Each rule file starts with a three-line YAML frontmatter block telling Cursor when to attach the file. For communication rules that should apply in every composer and chat session, set alwaysApply: true:

--- description: Communication preferences from AgentTune alwaysApply: true --- ## How to communicate with me - Show the code or minimal diff first, followed by a brief note on non-obvious choices. - Use plain prose for explanations; skip conversational intros and closing summaries. - Flag breaking changes, edge cases, or missing tests in one sentence before applying edits. - Ask for clarification only when an ambiguity changes the public interface or data model.

remember that files inside .cursor/rules/ are often tracked in git. If you work on a shared repository and want your personal communication rules to stay private to your machine, add .cursor/rules/personal-*.mdc to .git/info/exclude or place personal tone preferences in Cursor's user-level Rules for AI setting.

GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, and on GitHub.com automatically reads .github/copilot-instructions.md at the root of your repository. Because that file is shared by every contributor on the repository, keep the communication section focused on team-friendly clarity rules alongside your build and test commands:

## Communication & review style - Lead with the proposed fix or root cause before explaining background context. - Prefer small, targeted diffs over unrelated refactors. - State assumptions explicitly when test coverage or types are incomplete. - Skip filler openings and generic sign-offs in chat and pull request summaries.

sections.h2: 3. Gemini CLI and Code Assist: GEMINI.md.
sections.html: Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist read ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md for your personal defaults and GEMINI.md in the repository root for project context. Putting your personal AgentTune profile in ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md keeps your voice consistent across every project without touching git history. See our full Google Gemini personality guide for details on combining GEMINI.md with Gems and Saved info.

sections.h2: Exporting any of the 43 AgentTune profiles in one click.
sections.html: On every profile page in the AgentTune library, choose Coding assistant in the first dropdown of the prompt picker, then pick Cursor · project rule, GitHub Copilot · repository instructions, Gemini CLI · GEMINI.md, Claude Code · output style, or Codex · personal instructions. The picker automatically wraps your selected tuning in the exact frontmatter and comments required by that tool.

faq.a: Yes. Cursor uses .cursor/rules/*.mdc files with YAML frontmatter (description, globs, and alwaysApply: true/false) so projects can separate always-on rules from file-pattern rules.

faq.q: Where do I put personal communication rules so I don't commit them to a team repo?
faq.a: Use ~/.codex/AGENTS.md in OpenAI Codex, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or ~/.claude/output-styles/ in Claude Code, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md in Gemini CLI, or user-level Rules for AI in Cursor Settings.

faq.q: Can I use the same AgentTune tuning across Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex?
faq.a: Yes. The core bullet points are portable across all coding assistants; only the file path and YAML frontmatter (such as alwaysApply: true for Cursor or keep-coding-instructions: true for Claude Code) differ.
